source.title: Neonatal chronic hind paw inflammation alters sensitization to intradermal capsaicin in adult rats: a behavioral and immunocytochemical study.

confidence_rationale: Strong, mechanistically detailed rodent study with a developmental-window dissociation (P0 inflammation permanently sensitizes adult pain; P14 inflammation does not). It cuts two ways for ARC-046: it confirms the failure mode ARC-046 is designed to prevent is real (unprotected early harm produces permanent, catastrophic sensitization -- 'residue saturation' that survives into adulthood), and it confirms a developmental WINDOW exists (supporting progressive removal of protection). But it also pressures the optimistic half of ARC-046 -- the assumption that early harm exposure can be reliably educative-without-damage -- by showing that timing alone determines whether identical insults are benign or permanently damaging. Hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Early (P0) nociceptive insult produces lasting adult hyperalgesia + central sensitization (Fos up-regulation in dorsal horn) -- i.e. harm exposure WITHOUT protection causes exactly the catastrophic residue saturation ARC-046 posits.
The benign-vs-damaging outcome depends entirely on developmental timing (P0 damages, P14 does not), so an infant-protection mechanism that mis-times the protection window would fail.
If REE's residue_scale_factor attenuation were applied uniformly rather than within a critical window, it would not match the window-specific biology this paper documents.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Unilateral hind-paw inflammation (CFA) delivered on postnatal day 0 produces increased capsaicin-evoked thermal and mechanical hyperalgesia, allodynia, and increased dorsal-horn Fos expression in adulthood; the same insult delivered on P14 does not. Neonatal chronic inflammation initiated within a critical developmental period permanently alters adult pain sensitivity via lasting central sensitization.
mapping.ree_translation: The neonatal nociceptive pathways are demonstrably active and plastic during infancy (consistent with ARC-046's z_harm_s/z_harm_a 'fire normally'), but an unprotected early harm insult does not merely teach harm geography -- it permanently raises the gain of the harm system into adulthood. This is the biological instantiation of 'catastrophic residue saturation': harm load during a sensitive window leaves a durable, maladaptive set-point. It therefore grounds the NEED for ARC-046's residue_scale_factor / reduced hazard_magnitude, while warning that the protection must be window-timed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures peripheral/spinal nociceptive sensitization, not a global 'residue field', and the damaging outcome here is hyperalgesia (raised gain), whereas ARC-046's residue saturation is framed as accumulation that exhausts behavioral plasticity. These are related but not identical failure modes. The P0-vs-P14 dissociation also concerns the rat spinal nociceptive system specifically; mapping its critical-period boundaries onto REE's infancy->childhood curriculum is qualitative. Direction is mixed, not 'supports', because the same data tension ARC-046's optimistic premise (educative-without-damage) against its protective premise (damage is real and must be clamped).
mapping.source_context: Rodent behavioral + immunocytochemical study (J Pain) on developmental programming of adult pain by neonatal inflammatory insult, within the Fitzgerald-era literature on critical periods in the developing nociceptive system.

confidence_components.notes: Good empirical rodent study with a clean within-paper developmental dissociation. Mapping fidelity moderate -- it speaks directly to the failure mode (catastrophic, lasting harm-system change) but via spinal hyperalgesia rather than a residue analog. Transfer risk elevated (rat spinal cord -> REE residue architecture).
